h1:
Lampang in 1 Day
Old Town – Temple – Cafes
intro: Lampang is a town you can see in a single day without rushing, as long as you order the stops well. Head out in the morning to the temple of Wat Phra That Lampang Luang just outside town, swing back mid-morning to walk the old town along the Wang River, sip coffee in an old wooden house in the afternoon, and cap the day at Kad Kong Ta. This is a plan you can actually follow, with opening hours we've checked.

blocks.html: Lampang is just the right size for a day trip. The main sights aren't far apart — it's about 18 km from town to Wat Phra That Lampang Luang, only 25–30 minutes by car, while the old town, Kad Kong Ta, and the cafes are all within walking distance of each other in one neighbourhood. The trick is to do the out-of-town stop (the temple) in the morning while the sun is still soft, then ease back into town mid-morning so you're not zigzagging back and forth.

blocks.title: Before you set out
blocks.html: If you don't have your own car, you can rent a motorbike in town for around ฿250–300 a day, or hire a songthaew/taxi to Wat Phra That Lampang Luang and back. Agree on the price before you get in — it saves hassle. The horse-drawn carriages are great for short sightseeing loops around the old town, but not for running out of town.

blocks.text: Morning — Wat Phra That Lampang Luang

blocks.html: Start the day with Lampang's headline sight. Wat Phra That Lampang Luang sits in Ko Kha district, about 18 km southwest of town, and is one of the most beautiful and best-preserved Lanna temples in the North. The main viharn is open-sided with no walls, and the golden chedi stands tall on a low hill. Climb the naga staircase and you reach a wide, quiet courtyard.

items.activity: Leave central Lampang and drive to Wat Phra That Lampang Luang
items.note: About 18 km, 25–30 min. You can grab coffee or patongko along the way.

items.activity: Pay respects at the temple; explore the main viharn, Viharn Nam Taem, and the Phra Chao Lan Thong shrine
items.note: The temple opens early, around 07:30–17:00, free entry. Mornings have lovely light and fewer people.

items.activity: Look for the famous upside-down image of the chedi in the Buddha viharn (projected through a small hole in the wall)
items.note: A little-known corner many people miss. Ask staff to point out the spot — no entry fee.
Before the heat builds, timed nicely for a late breakfast in town.

blocks.title: What to wear
blocks.html: This is an old temple still used for active worship, so dress modestly — nothing too short, no bare shoulders — and take off your shoes before entering the viharn. The old wooden floors can be slippery, so watch your step.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Lampang trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Lampang
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: Late morning–midday — Khao soi, then the old town

blocks.html: Back in town, refuel with northern Thai food first. Lampang is known for khao soi and gaeng hang lay, with both long-running shops and atmospheric wooden-house spots. Once you're full, walk it off in the old town along the Wang River — a neighbourhood that packs temples, antique wooden houses, and characterful little shops all within walking distance.

items.activity: Late breakfast of northern food — khao soi, gaeng hang lay, or a Lampang nam prik set
items.note: Well-known spots include Khao Soi Islam (nearly 70 years old) or Gaeng Hom Cafe in a wooden garden house.

items.activity: Visit Wat Phra Kaeo Don Tao Suchadaram, a 500-year-old temple on the Wang River
items.note: It once housed the Emerald Buddha; the Burmese-style carvings are beautiful.

items.activity: Stop by Baan Sao Nak, a teak house over 100 years old
items.note: Named for its many pillars (sao). There's a small entry fee, around ฿30–50, to see how Lampang people lived in the old days.

items.activity: Stroll the old market street around Kad Kong Ta to see the wooden and gingerbread-style buildings
items.note: Most shops aren't open during the day, but it's great for photographing the architecture.

blocks.text: Afternoon — Horse carriage and a wooden-house cafe

blocks.html: The afternoon is when Lampang is at its most charming. As the sun softens, it's a good time for a horse-drawn carriage ride around town — a Lampang signature you won't find anywhere else in Thailand — followed by a coffee stop. Cafes here range from old wooden houses by the river to minimalist spots in the Kad Kong Ta area. Pick one and rest your legs.

items.activity: Take a short horse-carriage loop past the temples and old houses along the Wang River
items.note: The main carriage stand is by the old city hall / Wienglakor Hotel · a chartered loop starts around ฿200–300.

items.activity: Cafe break with coffee and a snack, out of the afternoon sun
items.note: Pick from the cafe list below — there are riverside-view spots and ones inside Kad Kong Ta.

items.activity: Shop for souvenirs — rooster bowls and Lampang ceramics
items.note: There are ceramic shops in town and along Phahonyothin Road; pick a nice piece to take home.

blocks.text: Cafes in Lampang town to drop into during the day

blocks.html: Pick one of these for your afternoon break. Most are in the old town–Kad Kong Ta area, all within walking distance, with coffee in the ฿55–90 range, typical for a provincial-town cafe.

items.name: At One Kad Kong Ta
items.blurb: A cafe in an old building in the Kad Kong Ta area, with its standout second-floor balcony looking out over Lampang town. There's coffee, breakfast, pizza, and desserts, and you can linger for hours from morning till evening.

items.name: Tim Pang Nom Sod Kad Kong Ta
items.blurb: A classic, vintage-style spot for fresh milk, toast, and ice cream on the walking-street strip. Good for a light, cool-down dessert at friendly prices.

items.name: Pang Suree Art Home
items.blurb: A white house decorated with local folk art, with plenty of photo corners and a quiet, easygoing feel. A nice place to chill and take photos in the old town.

items.name: Chaosua Tea Room & Homestay
items.blurb: A tea room in an old house with a Chinese–Lanna feel, serving tea and desserts; it's also a homestay. Open until evening on weekdays, and later into the night on weekends.

blocks.text: Evening — Kad Kong Ta walking street

blocks.html: Cap the day at Kad Kong Ta, the Saturday–Sunday walking street in the old market quarter along the Wang River. It has the feel of an old Chinese market, with wooden buildings lining both sides and plenty of local food, souvenirs, crafts, and kids' toys to browse. This is where locals and visitors alike come to walk in the evening.

items.activity: Start walking Kad Kong Ta, the riverside walking street
items.note: Open only Sat–Sun, around 17:00–22:00 · if you come on a weekday, skip it and have dinner in town instead.

items.activity: Find dinner — sample street food and local snacks
items.note: Khao kaep (rice crackers), sai ua, khanom jeen nam ngiao, and fried bites are all on offer from several vendors.

items.activity: One last souvenir run, then head back to your room
items.note: Crafts and ceramics in the market make good small gifts.

blocks.title: If you come on a weekday
blocks.html: Kad Kong Ta is only in full swing on Saturday and Sunday. If you come Monday–Friday, the area is quiet, so swap dinner for a northern-food restaurant in town, or a cafe that stays open late, like At One.

blocks.text: Route and budget recap for 1 day

items: Morning — Wat Phra That Lampang Luang (Ko Kha), free entry
Late morning–midday — Northern meal + Wat Phra Kaeo Don Tao + Baan Sao Nak + old-town walk
Afternoon — Horse carriage + wooden-house cafe + ceramic souvenirs
Evening — Kad Kong Ta (Sat–Sun) or a restaurant in town
Overall budget per person — around ฿600–1,000 including food, the carriage, a cafe, and a few small souvenirs (excluding vehicle rental)

blocks.html: All of this fits comfortably into a single day. If you have more time, Lampang also has the Thai Elephant Conservation Center, Wat Chaloem Phra Kiat (a temple on a mountain ridge), and Chae Son National Park to add on the following day.

faq.a: It's enough for the main highlights — Wat Phra That Lampang Luang, the riverside old town, a horse-carriage ride, a cafe, and Kad Kong Ta. If you order it so the out-of-town stop comes in the morning and you sightsee in town afterward, you won't get worn out or have to double back.

faq.q: What time does Wat Phra That Lampang Luang open, and is there an entry fee?
faq.a: It's open daily around 07:30–17:00 and entry is free. It sits in Ko Kha district, about 18 km from central Lampang. Go in the morning, when the sun is still soft and there are fewer people.

faq.q: What days is Kad Kong Ta open?
faq.a: Kad Kong Ta is a walking street open only on Saturday and Sunday evenings, around 17:00–22:00. If you come on a weekday the area is quiet, so switch to dinner at a restaurant in town or a cafe that stays open late instead.

faq.q: Do you need your own vehicle to see Lampang town?
faq.a: The old town is walkable and has horse carriages, but Wat Phra That Lampang Luang is 18 km out of town, so you'll need transport. We'd suggest renting a motorbike for around ฿250–300 a day, or hiring a songthaew there and back — agree on the price before you get in.

faq.q: What's the best time of year to visit Lampang?
faq.a: November to February has cool, comfortable weather, best for outdoor sightseeing. In the rainy season the temple and old town turn lush and green, but bring an umbrella. Avoid March–April, when northern Thailand can have haze problems.
